US-517 DONE (Sprint 69 / V0.29.24, 8/11). Config binding + validator default + HomeLocationProvider read path for pi.location.home.{lat,lon,elevationM}. Commit below.

THE ONE THE NEXT AGENT MUST KNOW BEFORE TOUCHING US-518 (next by priority): deploy-pi.sh EXCLUDES .env from the deploy payload (lines 190/217/225; the only thing deploy writes there is COMPANION_API_KEY at line 430). The Pi keeps its OWN .env, so the PI_HOME_* values Iris put in the dev checkout DO NOT propagate. On the Pi the placeholders stay unresolved and the provider correctly reports unknown. Therefore US-518's altitude re-anchor is a NO-OP ON THE PI until someone writes those three lines into the Pi's .env. Still correct to build -- it resets when the anchor is known and does nothing when it is not -- but do NOT promise live validation of US-518 on the strength of its code. I did not add a deploy step: out of scope, and writing location PII to the box is a CIO call. 3 options + a recommendation are in pm/inbox.

THE STRUCTURAL TRAP, general to EVERY ${...}-bound config key, not just this one: secrets_loader.resolveSecrets leaves the placeholder VERBATIM when the env var is unset with no inline default. So '${PI_HOME_LAT}' is a TRUTHY, NON-None string in the validated config, which means the validator's None default NEVER FIRES on a real Pi. The consumer is what has to absorb it. Report the actual remedy ('set X in this host's .env'), not a generic parse error -- an unresolved placeholder and a typo'd number have different fixes. Routed to Atlas as a possible standing rule.

DELIBERATE INCONSISTENCY, flagged to Atlas for a possible NAK: NO fail-fast validator sub-check for this section, unlike pi.homeNetwork / pi.companionService. validate() runs on the Pi's BOOT PATH, so raising over a typo in an OPTIONAL altitude anchor would refuse to start the orchestrator -- a dead OBD capture traded for a cosmetic fault (I-038 shape). Follows pi.power.mode (US-421): tolerate in the validator, honest unknown at the provider. 4 tests pin that validate() does NOT raise.

PII DISCIPLINE (the story's actual point): this is the FIRST config section whose VALUES may never be committed. Bare placeholders only -- I deliberately did NOT use the ${VAR:default} form the rest of config.json uses, because a fallback coordinate is BOTH committed PII AND a fabricated anchor; a regex test now fails loudly on any ':' default. The provider never logs a coordinate value (PIIMaskingFilter masks email/phone/SSN only). WATCH THIS ONE: my own first draft of the never-log-PII test used the CIO's REAL latitude as its fixture. The guard needed an OUT-OF-RANGE value (91.5) to trigger the warning anyway. When you test a PII rule, check the FIXTURE is fake before you check the assertion is right.

43 tests, all RED first for the right reason (one of the 12 binding tests passed immediately -- it guards Iris's existing .env.example lines from deletion, stated plainly rather than counted as new coverage). 3 mutations proved; the informative one: deleting the unresolved-placeholder branch leaves the returnsNone test GREEN (float('${...}') raises anyway) and ONLY the log-MESSAGE test catches it -- when a guard's outcome is identical to the fallback's, the message is the only observable difference. Also: float('nan')/float('inf') SUCCEED, and float(True)==1.0 reads as a plausible sea-level anchor.

Green in-loop: tests/pi/location + tests/test_home_location_config_binding.py + tests/test_config_validator.py + tests/common = 133 passed, exit 0; ruff clean; python validate_config.py = all passed.

PRE-EXISTING FAILURE, NOT MINE -- TD-073 FILED: tests/lint/test_ralph_promise_tag_contract.py fails on this branch (prompt.md documents COMPLETE + PARTIAL_BLOCKED, ralph.sh has no branches for them). Both files unmodified by me. It is in the FAST lint suite so it WILL fail the PM integration gate at close, and COMPLETE is the tag that ENDS a sprint -- same shape as the US-513 finding (a test asserting a contract against the artifact that DESCRIBES the behaviour, not the one that ENFORCES it). Needs a look, not a rubber stamp.

SPRINT STATE: 8 done (US-501/502/503/504b/505/512/513/517). Remaining: US-504a (needs-ruling, STILL BLOCKED on 2 rulings -- PM/Atlas orphan policy + Spool gate/band overlap; do NOT start), US-518 (next by priority, ready -- read the no-op caveat above), US-521 gyro-fused pitch.
